source_review.notes: Checked all six structured references at the OpenID Foundation or RFC Editor. OIDC Core and Discovery are the final 1.0 specifications incorporating errata set 2 dated 15 December 2023. Core confirms OIDC as an identity layer, ID-token/subject/UserInfo/nonce/auth_time/acr/amr semantics. RFC 8725 supports mutually exclusive JWT profiles; RFC 9068 distinguishes JWT access tokens; RFC 9700 supplies current OAuth security context; RP-Initiated Logout supplies the explicitly scoped logout profile.

evidence: Reviewed authentication context C, ID-token predicate V_ID, API predicate V_AT, local policy P, principal pair p=(iss,sub), and request/resource/state symbols for consistent definitions.
Confirmed aud membership, azp, time, nonce, auth_time, acr/amr, and claim/provenance terminology follows the distinct RP and resource-server roles.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The notation uses GitHub-compatible delimiters and makes the central non-substitution invariant visible: V_ID does not imply V_AT or local allow.

numerical_recomputation.notes: No quantitative identity assurance probability, entropy estimate, performance benchmark, or loss computation is claimed. The executable timestamps exercise exact deterministic policy boundaries only.

evidence: Expanded V_ID into cryptographic, exact issuer, client audience/azp, expiration/issued-at, nonce, and auth_time/acr/amr policy predicates and matched each to the numbered validator.
Re-derived allow(x)=V_AT and local P(context,request,resource,state), confirming a valid RP ID token cannot satisfy the API access-token predicate.
Checked equality of external principals requires the ordered exact pair (iss,sub), not either string or profile claims.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The symbolic relationships remain definitions of boundary policy and do not claim all OPs share assurance semantics.

evidence: Reviewed ID/access/refresh token substitution, wrong issuer/key/algorithm/audience/azp/nonce/time, discovery/key URL SSRF, mix-up, stale keys, and metadata outage.

Reviewed identical sub across issuers, pairwise subjects, changed/recycled/unverified email, auto-linking/login CSRF, JIT duplicate races, issuer migration, disabled/deprovisioned accounts, and UserInfo subject mismatch.
Reviewed iat versus auth_time, unknown/downgraded acr, misleading amr, wrong-subject/action step-up, tenant header crossing, stale groups, and independent logout/session/token/provisioning states.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Adversarial review covers both cryptographic artifact substitution and semantic identity/authorization confusion across the complete lifecycle.

evidence: Executed oidc-id-token-policy: valid context accepted; wrong orders-api audience, wrong nonce, stale authentication, unapproved acr, and multiple-audience wrong azp were independently rejected.
Checked exact time predicate iat <= now < exp and maximum authentication age based on auth_time rather than token issue freshness.
invariant_checking.notes: The finite model intentionally assumes cryptographic validation and is labeled as non-JOSE/non-OAuth evidence; production libraries and full profile tests remain required.

proof_review.notes: No formal identity, cryptographic, protocol-composition, or authorization proof is claimed. The module states the external trust and operational dependencies bounding its assurance argument.

evidence: Confirmed OIDC standards requirements, local policy mappings, contextual design recommendations, and lifecycle limitations are separated.
Confirmed the mechanism explicitly bounds security by OP trust, registration, OAuth flow, libraries, discovery/keys, account lifecycle, authorization, time, and operations.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: The chapter never elevates JWT signature validity, email verification, amr count, consent, or an executable claims model into proof of identity or permission.

evidence: Snippet report artifacts/snippets/API-044/report.json records one passing deterministic local ID-token policy execution.

Real JOSE/OIDC, discovery, UserInfo, browser transaction, account-link, lifecycle, outage, privacy, and incident tests are presented as future verification obligations, not completed deployment measurements.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No live OP, RP, API, directory, logout channel, penetration test, or real identity assurance was empirically assessed.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed protocol/role distinctions, artifact matrix, issuer bootstrap, transaction and ID-token validation, subject identity, linking, claim provenance, UserInfo, assurance/freshness, contexts, tenants/authorization, sessions/logout/provisioning, privacy, errors, and tests as a coherent boundary model.

practitioner_review.notes: Checked deployability for multi-issuer metadata/key caches, RP/BFF/API separation, local principal schemas, pairwise subjects, JIT and enterprise provisioning, step-up transactions, local tenant policy, independent logout/revocation SLAs, safe observability, and emergency key/issuer migration. Product-specific assurance mappings remain explicit governed configuration.

pedagogical_review.notes: The module starts with a recipient matrix and one non-substitution rule, then builds identity, claims, assurance, tenant, and lifecycle reasoning. Ten examples isolate common boundary errors; five exercises synthesize artifact validation, schema/linking, step-up, migration, and lifecycle testing with detailed answers.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
